item.title: Trump owned millions in Nvidia stock as he pressed for Jensen Huang's reinstatement
item.description: President Trump holds tens of millions in Nvidia shares, giving him a personal stake in the company's stock market roller coaster ride of the past two weeks, financial disclosure documents show.

item.title: Army detonates toxic explosives at Iowa plant despite concerns
item.description: The U.S. Army detonated a stockpile of degrading explosives at a munitions plant in Iowa on Wednesday, after days of back-and-forth between politicians and the courts.

item.title: Maps show where Thanksgiving storms could disrupt holiday
item.description: Rain, snow and powerful winds were forecast to impact large stretches of the country on Thanksgiving, potentially disrupting holiday festivities and, in some areas, hampering travel plans.

item.title: Judge temporarily blocks FCC from reviewing ABC's licenses
item.description: A federal judge blocked the FCC from moving forward with an early review of ABC's broadcast licenses, a move the network argues is an attempt by the Trump administration to punish speech it does not like.

item.title: A look at the probes involving Nvidia, Jensen Huang and Megaspeed
item.description: The reinstatement of Jensen Huang as president and CEO of Nvidia sent shockwaves through the political and business world, and has fueled scrutiny by Congress.

item.title: Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade postponed for 1st time in history
item.description: For the first time in history, the Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade has been postponed due to weather, Macy's said Wednesday.

item.title: Jennifer Lopez's choreographer on what to expect from "The JLo Show"
item.description: Kiel Tutin, supervising choreographer for "The JLo Show," joins "The Daily Report" to discuss the film and Jennifer Lopez's intense Las Vegas residency. "The JLo Show" premieres Thursday night on CBS and Paramount+. Paramount+ is owned by CBS News' parent company, Skydance.

item.title: Butterball Turkey hotline ramps up staffing, prepared to help with Thanksgiving cooking needs
item.description: Even in the world of email, texting and artificial intelligence, the Butterball Turkey hotline has only gotten more popular. The larger team is prepared to field about 100,000 calls this holiday season to help with any turkey troubles. Tony Dokoupil has the story.

item.title: Thieves steal cufflinks, clock from British royal estate
item.description: Two Albanian men were accused of breaking into the country home of Prince William and Princess Kate. Holly Williams reports.

item.title: As Thanksgiving meal costs rise, food donation lines get longer
item.description: At the home of the Dallas Cowboys, thousands of cars inched across the massive parking lot as volunteers filled truck beds with turkeys, potatoes, cabbage and carrots. The cost of a Thanksgiving meal is even more expensive this year, creating more demand from families in need. Jason Allen has more.

item.title: Trump blames volatile stock market on midterm election results
item.description: President Trump blamed the volatile stock market on the midterm election results that will put Democrats in control of Congress in January. Weijia Jiang has more.

item.title: Judge declines to issue long-term ban on tax-funded pro-Trump ads
item.description: A federal judge has sided against Democrats on the federal government's taxpayer-funded political ads, which critics say were illegal propaganda intended to promote President Trump.

item.title: EPA detects no lead in air shortly after toxic Iowa chemical detonation
item.description: The Army went through with blowing up five tons of an old bomb-making chemical at a plant in Iowa on Wednesday, hoping to control the potential for a cloud of lead dust. Ian Lee reports.

item.title: Steelers release Aaron Rodgers after tirade following benching
item.description: Quarterback Aaron Rodgers, a four-time NFL MVP, was benched by the Pittsburgh Steelers and then cut hours after an interview in which he accused head coach Mike McCarthy of sleeping through meetings. Mark Strassmann has more details.

item.title: Food banks see surge in visits amid rising Thanksgiving costs
item.description: Some food banks are having to restock supplies as more families look for assistance ahead of this year's Thanksgiving festivities. CBS News' Jason Allen reports.

item.title: King tides cause monster waves, flooding on California coastline
item.description: Tuesday night's full moon supercharged king tides in the West, causing flooding in several of California's coastal communities. Matt Gutman reports.

item.title: Trump owned millions in Nvidia stock while pushing for Jensen Huang's reinstatement
item.description: Financial disclosures reveal that President Trump holds tens of millions of dollars worth of Nvidia shares, giving him a personal stake in the company's recent roller coster ride in the stock market. CBS News' Isabel Vincent has more.

item.title: Thanksgiving holiday travel chaos in full swing amid stormy weather
item.description: A "passenger disturbance" prompted a Chicago-bound flight to divert to Phoenix on Wednesday, federal officials said. Meanwhile, Thanksgiving travelers crowded airports and some raced against Mother Nature as a storm moves up the East Coast. Kris Van Cleave reports.

item.title: At least 31 killed after fuel tanker crashes and catches fire near Cairo
item.description: A crash involving a fuel tanker has ignited a massive fire on a major highway surrounding Cairo, killing at least 31 people.

item.title: How people are using AI to cancel subscriptions, claim refunds
item.description: People are using AI agents to handle tedious tasks that could save them money. CBS News' Megan Cerullo explains.

item.title: Details on why Macy's postponed its Thanksgiving Day Parade
item.description: The Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade, watched by tens of millions of people, including those lining the streets of New York, has been postponed because of weather for the first time ever. Organizers made the announcement Wednesday, just hours after inflating those infamous balloons. Tom Hanson reports and Rob Marciano has the forecast.

item.title: Watch: Kilmar Abrego Garcia arrives in Spain after leaving U.S.
item.description: Kilmar Abrego Garcia, who was mistakenly deported and sent to a prison in El Salvador last year, has left the U.S. for Spain. CBS News' Camilo Montoya-Galvez has more.

item.title: Videos capture Army's detonation of explosives in Iowa
item.description: The Army conducted its planned detonation of unstable bomb-making materials in Iowa on Wednesday. CBS News' Ian Lee reports.

item.title: Andy Taylor, longtime Duran Duran guitarist, dies at 65
item.description: Andy Taylor, the original guitarist of the 1980s English new wave band Duran Duran, has died at age 65 following a battle with prostate cancer.

item.title: 11/25: CBS Evening News
item.description: Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade is postponed until Saturday; Thanksgiving travelers rush to beat bad weather.

item.title: U.S.-based firms helping China access Nvidia's most advanced chips
item.description: It's not just Megaspeed. A CBS News investigation reveals that at least two California-based Nvidia customers have Chinese ownership — giving the U.S. adversary potential access to Nvidia's most advanced technology.

item.title: How a new generation of AI agents could change holiday shopping
item.description: The internet revolutionized holiday shopping by allowing people to make purchases without leaving their homes. Now, a new generation of AI agents is promising an even bigger change: Doing the shopping for you. Jared Ochacher reports on what to look out for if you're planning to hand over your holiday list to an AI agent this year.

item.title: 11/25: The Takeout with Major Garrett
item.description: Weather postpones Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade; Trump introduces new tariffs on China, the EU and major trading partners.

item.title: Why are investors freaking out even as the U.S. economy surges?
item.description: The economy is sending mixed signals, with growth jumping while stocks gyrate. Here's what economists say is going on.

item.title: Butterball hotline expert shares cooking tips for a delicious Thanksgiving turkey
item.description: For those taking the lead in the kitchen this Thanksgiving, it can be a lot of pressure to deliver that juicy, well-seasoned turkey. Mary Alice Coffey, an expert with Butterball's Turkey Talk-Line, joins CBS News with cooking tips.
